To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spontaneous activity of cutaneously driven neurons of the spinal cord dorsal horn of cats is low and that it is not affected by cord transection.
the spontaneous activity of neurons in the cutaneous spinal dorsal-horn is minimal or nonexistent, both before and after spinal cord transection.
spinal dorsal horn neurons have a very low rate of spontaneous firing, and the lack of spontaneous firing is not altered by spinal transection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods of spinal cord injury repair and regeneration, and the mechanisms of spinal cord injury and regeneration.
the role that the spinal cord plays in the control of pain.
understanding the role of sensory inputs in the generation of spontaneous activity in spinal dorsal horn neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spontaneous activity of cutaneoafferent neurons is not present in the chronic spinal cat, but may be present in the acute preparation.
in chronic spinal cats, cutaneous dorsal horn neurons are not spontaneously active.
the spontaneous activity of cuticular dorsal horn neurons is minimal or nonexistent in awake, drugfree, spinal-cord-transected cats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spinal cord is a very active place in acute preparations, but that this activity is greatly diminished in the chronic, awake state.
the spinal cord in the awake, drug-free animal does not appear to have a significant role in the generation of spontaneous activity.
the spinal cord of the cat, when intact and functioning, does not generate a spontaneous activity in the dorsal horn neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spinal cord is capable of producing a wide range of behaviors in a chronic, awake, and drug-free state.
the lack of spontaneous firing is a feature of the dorsal horn of awake, drug free, spinally transection cats.
the lack of spontaneous activity in the chronic preparation suggests a role for descending influences on the spontaneous firing rate of dorsal horn cells.
